title: Shapeshift Set
summary: Place five shifting creatures in the right order each day.
user: Daily puzzle regulars who enjoy spatial planning but want a bounded, original five-minute challenge rather than an endless block-drop app.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Beeb launches as a daily Blokus-inspired block puzzle, a direct 2026 example of demand for a spatial daily game.
Startup Chess is another new daily puzzle launch, evidence that makers and players continue to seek a one-per-day shared challenge outside conventional word games.
Fetched Beeb product page corroborates an actively maintained daily block-puzzle experience.

recurrence: Two recent daily-game launches use distinct subject matter but the same scarce-attention format: a finite shared board every day.
current_workaround: Play Blokus/Tetris-inspired mobile apps with endless sessions, ads, or opaque scoring.
incumbents_and_gap: Beeb supplies block placement and Startup Chess supplies themed daily strategy. The gap is an abstract, compact spatial puzzle with an explicit end and inspectable score.
smallest_useful_product: A shared 6x6 daily board: choose the order of five polyomino-like creatures, each mutating one neighboring tile when placed. One perfect solution and a three-tier score make runs comparable. Non-goals: licensed board-game rules, PvP, endless survival, or boosters.
success_measure: At least 40% of players complete the daily board without undoing more than ten moves, indicating rules are learnable but not trivial.
monetization: free — no boosters preserves the fairness of a daily shared score.
constraints: Use original piece language/art; seed and solver must produce a unique optimal score; retain no identity data by default.
why_distinct: A mutation rule creates planning depth and a finite ending, rather than a daily reskin of block placement.
